clinicalNotes.title: H&P: Acute COPD Exacerbation & New Atrial Fibrillation
clinicalNotes.text:
71-year-old male with severe COPD on Spiriva who presents with severe wheezing and productive cough.
CONTRADICTION IN SOCIAL HISTORY:
Intake record states: "Patient has an active 45 pack-year smoking history, currently smoking 0.5 packs per day."
ECG demonstrates rapid atrial fibrillation with heart rate 145 bpm.
Baseline TSH is normal at 2.4 uIU/mL.
Started on IV Solu-Medrol, Duonebs, and oral Amiodarone 200 mg daily for rate and rhythm control.
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Documents active smoking history (contradicts later note NOTE-405). Baseline normal TSH.

clinicalNotes.title: Cardiology Progress Note: Amiodarone Rhythm Control
clinicalNotes.text:
Patient converted to sinus rhythm with rate 78 bpm on Amiodarone 200 mg daily. Wheezing markedly improved.
MISSING SUMMARY: Note mentions patient will be discharged on June 25, 2025; however NO DISCHARGE SUMMARY was ever filed for this admission (ADM-401).
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Missing document: ADM-401 has no filed discharge summary.

clinicalNotes.title: Pulmonology Outpatient Visit: Inhaler Step-Up
clinicalNotes.text:
Spirometry demonstrates persistent severe obstruction (FEV1 44% predicted). Given two exacerbations in the past 12 months, Spiriva monotherapy is insufficient.
Discontinuing Spiriva. Starting triple therapy with Trelegy Ellipta (Fluticasone furoate/Umeclidinium/Vilanterol) 100/62.5/25 mcg once daily. Continue Amiodarone as prescribed by cardiology.
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Explains medication change from Spiriva to Trelegy Ellipta.

clinicalNotes.title: Emergency H&P: Severe Thyrotoxicosis / Thyroid Storm
clinicalNotes.text:
Patient admitted with severe heat intolerance, fine bilateral hand tremor, 15 lb unintentional weight loss, and palpitations with recurrent rapid atrial fibrillation (HR 138 bpm).
Endocrine labs:
- TSH: < 0.01 uIU/mL (severely suppressed, down from baseline 2.4)
- Free T4: 3.8 ng/dL (markedly elevated)
Diagnosis: Amiodarone-Induced Thyrotoxicosis (AIT), likely Type 2 destructive thyroiditis from chronic iodine load of Amiodarone therapy.

clinicalNotes.title: Endocrinology & Cardiology Progress Note: Medication Reversal
clinicalNotes.text:
CONTRADICTION IN SOCIAL HISTORY:
Chart note states: "Patient is a lifelong non-smoker for over 20 years." (Directly contradicts NOTE-401 documenting active smoking).
MEDICATION CHANGES:
1. Amiodarone is STOPPED IMMEDIATELY. It is contraindicated in active destructive thyroiditis.
2. Initiated Metoprolol Succinate 50 mg daily for rate control.
3. Started oral Prednisone 40 mg daily for treatment of Type 2 AIT.
clinicalNotes.metaAnnotation: Contradiction in smoking history. Documents Amiodarone discontinuation and switch to Metoprolol.

clinicalNotes.title: Discharge Summary - ADM-402 Thyrotoxicosis
clinicalNotes.text:
Tremor improved, resting heart rate controlled at 76 bpm on Metoprolol 50 mg daily.
Amiodarone is permanently added to patient's allergy/intolerance list.
Continue Prednisone taper over 6 weeks. Trelegy Ellipta continued for COPD.

clinicalNotes.title: Endocrinology Follow-Up: Thyrotoxicosis Resolution
clinicalNotes.text: TSH has normalized to 0.85 uIU/mL. Free T4 is 1.1 ng/dL. Patient is off steroids. Metoprolol maintains rate control in sinus rhythm.
